title: Checkout Merge Repair
lede: Staff and admins can now review and consolidate duplicate open event checkouts into one auditable custody record, including an explicit choice when return times or reservation links differ.

stats.n: Explicit merge scope on the Checkouts list
Kiosk remains the checkout creation and scan surface

sections.heading: Capture status
sections.note: A matched before/after screenshot pair is intentionally not included. The local protected Checkouts route reached the app but could not render because this checkout has no DATABASE_URL or DIRECT_URL; production was not changed. The pair must be captured against a controlled authenticated fixture after deployment.

changes.h: Duplicate checkouts were stranded as separate list records
changes.was: The Checkouts list had no way to select two same-event open checkouts for repair, so a duplicate battery checkout remained split from the original custody record.
changes.now: Staff/admin users can select compatible open checkouts and choose Merge matching checkouts; separate kiosk handoff timestamps no longer block the repair, the checkbox and three-dot action sit in a shared top-right rail in card view, the oldest checkout survives, and the other records become cancelled history.

changes.h: A visible merge could lose physical custody history
changes.was: Reparenting only the visible item lines would risk leaving scan sessions, stock movements, numbered-unit allocations, photos, reports, and return activity attached to the cancelled source.
changes.now: One serializable transaction moves custody-linked rows, numbered battery units, bulk quantities, and live-activity references, then writes before/after audit receipts for the target and each source.

changes.h: Same event is necessary but not sufficient
changes.was: A broad same-title or same-person merge could combine different event windows, locations, people, or started/returned custody.
changes.now: Preview and mutation require exact event set, title, requester metadata, custody scope, and location; the modal resolves return-time and reservation-link differences explicitly, while partial, completed, excluded, duplicate, or already-returned custody remains blocked.

changes.h: Return/source mismatches stopped the repair before review
changes.was: The merge endpoint rejected checkouts as soon as their return windows or source reservation IDs differed, so an operator could not decide which context should survive.
changes.now: A dedicated modal lists the available return times, accepts an adjusted due-back, and lets staff choose the surviving reservation link. The selected time is checked against combined availability and recorded in due-date and merge audit history.

verification: Focused checkout suite: 15 tests pass across service, route, and merge UI/source contracts; the booking UI polish contracts add 5 passing layout/accessibility checks.
Lint/build: targeted ESLint, full ESLint, and npm run build:app pass; codemaps are current and git diff --check passes.
Full repository suite: 589 files pass, but 33 existing worktree failures remain in unrelated iOS, schedule, availability, reservation, and system-hardening areas; the new checkout suite is green.
Runtime: local route verification is blocked by the missing database connection environment; authenticated browser proof, deployment, and a controlled live-data merge remain open.
notes: This is an explicit repair action, not automatic deduplication. The UI only offers it for staff/admin users and compatible OPEN checkouts.

After compatible code is deployed, use the modal for Usman's selected rows and confirm the return time before committing the repair. Keep the same event, person/custody scope, location, and active-item checks in view.
The implementation is local only; no production data was modified and no deployment was performed.
